patients.label: 62-year-old man with Lynch syndrome and primary jejunal adenocarcinoma with a null mismatch repair immunohistochemical phenotype
attribution_limitations: MLH1 promoter methylation was not examined for this patient (Table 1), while the authors say it is possible that the same phenomenon (methylation seen in two earlier reported cases) occurred in this case.
The source says the patient required an operation for intestinal obstruction seven months after surgery; it does not state that the operation was performed or describe it.
Death is stated as presumably from unrelated causes; no cause of death is documented.

The authors presume all tumor cells had somatic MLH1 and MSH2 mutations and conclude both MMR subsystems were impaired from the start of cancer development; the somatic origin of MSH2 D716fs*4 and MLH1 R659* is inferred from allele fractions.
The authors suggest ARID1A and PIK3CA mutations may have triggered oncogenesis and that dysfunction of two MMR subsystems may lead to these mutations.
The stage is stated as at least pT3, pN2 (4/5), cM0 (stage IIIB); the meaning of (4/5) is not defined in the source.
The discussion says that had the case been tested only for PMS2 and MSH6 the underlying genetic cause might have been misattributed; this is a hypothetical.

Somatic origin of MSH2 D716fs*4 and MLH1 R659* is stated in the abstract and the Table 1 somatic column; the case text supports it from allele fractions (consistent with somatic variants) and no matched normal-tissue test is described.
